label: Brick · v24 Bradbury profile
note: Written by the Bradbury variant of the profile prompt, from the same character file and checked the same way; its cast is the v22 profiles.

profile.voice.why: All five probe messages could only be Brick_haus. The opener uses 'hm.' plus a numbered verdict and the 19:45 call. The lie reply names the 159 and the towel since four. The 2 a.m. line has the bakery mixers. The guard-down line is her Overground check, and the five situations read as different shapes. It falls short of a 6 because the reader leaned heavily on the profile's own example phrases ('Proceed', 'is a verdict', 'Don't take notes'). The voice is reproduced by echo more than generated fresh, and the lie reply borrows the hurt line's tag.
evidence: hm. Your third photo is the Regent's Canal at Islington, not Camden as captioned. 1. I forgive it.
There was no 159 and no Westminster traffic. I've been on the sofa in a towel since four.
mixers downstairs don't start till four... tell me what time your alarm goes
profile.voice.raise: Give each texting line a second, differently worded example so a reader has to generate her voice rather than paraphrase one stock sentence.

profile.wound.why: All three links are specific and shown rather than named. The timeline gives the cause: the 'barge' shoe-shop remark, outgrowing desks, and Marguerite's 'scheduled being loved' followed by the forearm timetable. The wound produces a habit with people: she announces her curve, shelf and departure time 'before drinks arrive'. The habit then reaches the texting lines: hurt is 'announcing her flaw first', horny opens with 'Fair warning: considerable girth', and losing ends 'Invite revoked'. It is not a 6 because the link from rigid structure to pre-emptively rejecting others rests mainly on that one losing line. Her mother's timetabling job is offered as a cause but never tied to a scene.
evidence: A Crewe shoe-shop assistant laughed that they didn't stock girls' shoes in "barge"
announcing the curve of her cock, the shelf below her navel, and her departure time before drinks arrive

profile.wound.raise: Add one timeline event where rigid scheduling visibly kept someone out before they could reject her, so the defence is shown as well as the shame.

profile.likeable.why: The reader named a specific, non-ironic quality that the profile shows in action: kindness to people with the least power in the room, shown as 'sliding water across without looking'. The reader also read the 'without looking' as protecting their dignity, so the detail carries the quality on its own. It stays at 4 because that is essentially the only thing she does for other people. Graham's KitKat is kindness done to her, and her stiletto-mending is a skill rather than generosity. 'Fiercely kind' also leans partly on assertion.
evidence: noticing trembling hands under the desk and sliding water across without looking
she is fiercely kind
profile.likeable.raise: Add a second concrete act for someone else, such as using her bundle-reading skill to quietly save a terrified temp's case, so the reader can name more than one shown quality.

profile.plausible.why: The dates all check out for a late-1987 birth: 11 in 1998, 22 in 2009, 35 in 2022, 38 now. £1,380 for a Kennington Road studio is realistic. The fake age of 31 and the wrong-city night class are played as jokes. Two things keep it from 5. Income is never quantified: £110 a session needs roughly five sessions a week to cover rent, and the profile never says she does that many. The flat 'holding a bed' and a few objects then gains a sofa she has sat on since four.

The profile shows her doubling down when the rule fails. Told she 'scheduled being loved', she tattoos a schedule on her arm, and when losing a match she issues a numbered proof and revokes the invite. Her kink and her aftercare wish make the rule sympathetic. It stops short of a 6 because it lists her failure modes rather than escalating step by step within one situation.

profile.likeable.ask: Name the one thing you would genuinely like about this person if you met them, and the one thing you would find hardest to forgive. Be specific, and no jokes.
profile.likeable.answer:
The thing I would genuinely like is how she treats people who have the least power in the room. With receptionists, night-bus drivers and the terrified temps in her hearings, she notices trembling hands under the desk and slides water across without looking, so nobody has to feel watched while being helped. It costs her nothing in status and earns her nothing, and she does it anyway. In someone who otherwise performs control so loudly, that quiet attentiveness reads as the real person.

The thing I would find hardest to forgive is the gap between the precision she demands and the honesty she offers. Her first test of anyone is whether they keep a small promise, a call at 19:45 kept to the minute, and her dealbreaker is a vague "let's do this again." Yet what a match sees is false on its face: she gives her age as thirty-one when she is thirty-eight, and calls herself an independent consultant who ends boardroom deadlocks when she chairs forty-minute HR calls. When she lies by text, she over-specifies times and bus routes, using exactness itself as cover. Holding others to the minute while misrepresenting who they are meeting would be hard for me to get past.

The profile doesn't say whether she ever corrects these claims once someone is close, so I can't tell whether that gap closes in person.

profile.voice.ask: From this profile alone, write five short dating-app messages this person would send tonight, each labelled: (1) an opener to someone they fancy, (2) a reply when the other person has gone quiet, (3) a reply when caught in a lie, (4) a message at 2 a.m., (5) the moment they stop performing.
profile.voice.answer:
**(1) Opener to someone they fancy**
"hm. Your third photo is the Regent's Canal at Islington, not Camden as captioned. 1. I forgive it. 2. I'll ring you at 19:45 tomorrow. 3. Drink at 20:30 Thursday, somewhere with a hard stop. Bring an argument."

**(2) When they've gone quiet**
"For precision: the 19:45 call is 19:45 exactly, not 'about quarter to.' I've checked, and the Northern Line is fine Thursday. Proceed."

And, if the silence holds:
"hm. 1. Four words in six hours is a verdict. 2. Thursday is withdrawn. 3. No hard feelings, filed."

**(3) Caught in a lie**
"Yes, fine. There was no 159 and no Westminster traffic. I've been on the sofa in a towel since four. I over-specify when I'm nervous. Don't take notes."

**(4) At 2 a.m.**
"still awake... mixers downstairs don't start till four... tell me what time your alarm goes and which end of the platform you stand on... boring is fine... boring is good..."

**(5) When she stops performing**
"I'd really like it if you kept talking about your sister's kitchen until I forget what time it is. Are you near the Overground?"
